title: private-deploy-field-notes-2026-03-04
content:
Daily scratchpad / field notes - Private deployments
Date: 2026-03-04
Owner: Jordan Lee
Context: Onsite kickoff for ACME Corp private deployment (VPC + on-prem gateway). Quick notes, blockers, and TODOs while pairing with Aisha.

High level status
- VM images staged in customer infra (2 x p4d for inference nodes, 1 x m5 for control plane).
- Control plane components deployed to internal VPC subnets (management-subnet).
- Initial smoke: api-gateway up, but worker pods crash-loop on kv-cache mount.

Top priority TODOs (today)
1) Fix kv-cache mount issue (blocking inference workers)
   - Hypothesis: NFS mount permissions or missing directory on host.
   - Quick checks: ssh to node -> sudo ls -la /var/redwood/kv-cache; check ownership (should be rw by redwood user uid 1101)
   - If missing: mkdir -p /var/redwood/kv-cache; chown 1101:1101 /var/redwood/kv-cache; systemctl restart redwood-worker.service
2) Confirm KMS integration for customer HSM (ACME-HSM)
   - Contact: ops@acme (Elena) for HSM network ACLs; need IP allowlist for control-plane management subnet (10.40.8.0/24)
   - Verify kube secret rotation policy matches their compliance window
3) Port & firewall checklist before final runbook
   - Control plane (management): 443, 8443 (api), 9646 (metrics) -> must be open to mgmt-subnet only
   - Worker to HSM: outbound 9443 (TLS) -> customer firewall must allow from worker-subnet (10.40.16.0/24)
   - Inference sick-checks use health endpoint on 5567 (local); ensure no external exposure
4) Certs: customer uses internal CA -> CSR flow
   - Generate CSR on control-plane host: /opt/redwood/bin/gen-csr --cn control.acme.internal
   - Upload to ACME internal CA portal (ticketed)

Observed errors & traces
- Worker logs: "Permission denied: cannot write to /var/redwood/kv-cache/locks/" -> indicates host FS perms.
- Control-plane logs: occasional 502 from api-gateway to model-router (timeout 30s) -> model-router OOM? Check pod memory (current limit/pod 2Gi).
- System: disk pressure on node-3 (inference-node-2) at 92% -> file cleanup + check metrics for model shards caching policy.

Temporary mitigations tried
- Created kv-cache dir and adjusted ownership (worked for one node, but other nodes have SELinux denial).
- Disabled SELinux enforcement for testing (setenforce 0) -> allowed worker start but need permanent policy (audit2allow)
- Increased model-router memory to 4Gi on canary -> network timeout reduced but still flaky under parallel requests

Follow-ups / long-running items
- SELinux: get selinux policy from infra team; create proper module to allow redwood-worker to write to /var/redwood/kv-cache (don't leave setenforce 0 in prod)
- Disk pressure: advise customer to mount larger ephemeral volume or tune cache retention (reduce model shard replicas)
- K8s node labels: attach label redwood.inference/zone=zone-b to worker nodes for routing policy

Rollback plan (if deployment causes customer service issues)
- Repoint api-gateway to hosted fallback (hosted.redwood.io) via DNS TTL change (5 min)
- Scale down worker deployment to 0, reattach previous customer-managed inference service if present
- Restore previous kube manifests from git tag release/2026-02-18

Questions for customer / blockers to resolve with ACME
- HSM network ACL: need explicit source CIDR for worker pool (they suggested 0.0.0.0/0 for testing, reject)
- SELinux baseline: can they allow auditd logs to be forwarded to our ops? They prefer to keep logs internal -> we need to coordinate for policy creation
- Certification authority: ETA on issuing control-plane cert (blocking final step)

Quick commands noted while debugging
- Check mounts: sudo mount | grep redwood
- Check SELinux denials: ausearch -m avc -ts recent; sudo cat /var/log/audit/audit.log | audit2allow -w -a
- Restart worker: sudo systemctl restart redwood-worker.service && journalctl -u redwood-worker -f --no-pager
- Increase model-router mem (k8s): kubectl -n redwood set resources deploy/model-router --limits=memory=4Gi --requests=memory=2Gi

Contacts / context
- ACME on-site: Elena Park (ops), +1 415-555-0192, elena.park@acme.example
- Sales AE: Marcus Holt (priority SLA)
- Internal: Aisha Patel (lead eng on private), Riley Nguyen (SRE)

Notes to self (todo after wrap)
- Convert these ad-hoc notes into runbook section: "KV cache host prep" and "SELinux policy for kv cache" in Confluence (CON-1423).
- Add small smoke test to post-install: create lock file in kv-cache and simulate worker start; include as part of installer CI
- Add checklist item: verify HSM cert trust chain and CRL distribution points are reachable from control-plane

End of notes.
